question.leadin: You probably know more about Hawaiian mythology than you think you do.
question.text: The menehune (MEN-eh-HOO-neh) are the Hawaiian equivalents of these little people that, in Norse mythology, make excellent smiths.
question.clue: Orange Alternative claimed there could be "no freedom without" what creatures? These creatures were graffitied in spots where Polish authorities had painted over anti-government messages.

swap.leadin: The term "Deluge" refers to a period in which Sweden occupied a union of these two countries, which was governed by a parliament called the sejm (same).
swap.text: Name these two countries that signed the 1569 Union of Lublin, unifying into a commonwealth that would last until it lost its land in a series of 18th century partitions.
swap.answerHtml: Poland and Lithuania [or the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, or Korona Królestwa Polskiego and Didi Kunigystė Lietuvos or the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]
swap.clue: The head of one of these countries instigated Zeligowski's Mutiny in the other.

question.leadin: One of these events in August 1980 was sparked by the firing of Anna Walentynowicz ["VAL-en-TIN-oh-WITCH"].
question.text: Name this type of action undertaken by workers at the Lenin Shipyards under the leadership of electrical engineer Lech Walesa ["WUH-leh-SUH"]. Arthur Scargill led several of these actions for British coal miners.
question.answerHtml: strikes [accept labor strikes or strike actions; prompt on protests or walkouts or factory occupations or industrial actions]
question.clue: The headline "Crisis? What Crisis?" was used to criticize James Callaghan's handling of a wave of these events that became known as the "Winter of Discontent."

swap.text: This man won the first free Polish election in 1990 after using his leverage as leader of Solidarity to push back Soviet influence at the Roundtable talks.
swap.clue: This man mourned his successor in 2010 after that successor died in a Smolensk airport plane crash.

question.leadin: One event in this modern-day nation was vehemently opposed by Tadeusz Reytan.
question.text: Name this nation which in 1772-1775 experienced its first partition by the Sejm [pr. SAME] Parliament, ending a commonwealth with Lithuania.
question.clue: A Senate was created here after the 1989 Round Table Agreement.

swap.text: Sigismund II's inability to bear a child resulted in the formation of this personal union partitioned by Prussia, Austria, and Russia. Napoleon later revived a small part of it as the Grand Duchy of Warsaw.
swap.clue: Monarchs agreed to the Henrician Articles and made individual commitments called the pacta conventa on becoming rulers of this country.

question.leadin: This country united with its neighbor Lithuania under the 1569 Union of Lublin.
question.text: Name this country, whose 1573 Compact of Warsaw guaranteed religious freedom to all free people within its borders.
question.clue: This country was united in the Union of Lublin while it was ruled by the Jagiellonians.

swap.leadin: During its country's first free election, this party used a modified version of a poster for the movie High Noon.
swap.text: Name this trade union founded by Lech Walesa that, in 1989, secured semi-free elections in a Warsaw Pact country.
swap.clue: Partly inspired by the 1971 essay Theses on Hope and Hopelessness, this organization secured its seat in government in a free election held in 1990, which led to a successful implementation of "shock therapy."

question.text: Stanislaus's daughter had married Louis XV, but he was sent to Lorraine by the French. The Spanish and Sardinians sought to undo the Peace of Utrecht, and therefore allied with the French against the Germans and Russians. For 15 points-name this 1733 to 1735 conflict which ended with confirmation of Augustus III's reign.
question.clue: The person who led the Confederation of Dzikow had previously held the job in question under Swedish domination and was the father-in-law of Louis XV.

swap.leadin: This event was engineered by Frederick the Great in order to avoid the expansion of a Russo-Turkish war.
swap.text: Identify this 1772 agreement that enlarged Russia, Prussia, and Austria at the expense of about one-third of another country's territory.
swap.answerHtml: the First Partition of Poland [prompt on partial answer]
swap.clue: This event was made possible following a victory at Lanckorona by Suvorov over the Confederation of Bar, which had attempted to depose Stanislaw II.

question.leadin: This man represented opposition groups at the Round Table Talks.
question.text: Name this electrician who led the trade union Solidarity.
question.clue: The KOR ("K-O-R") was a predecessor to an organization led by this man, which formed a coalition government with the PUWP.

swap.leadin: Twentieth-century Poland went through much turbulence.
swap.text: This former Socialist and editor of the newspaper Robotnik organized the Union of Riflemen to rebel against Russian rule during World War I and ruled newly independent as dictator from 1920 to 1922 and 1926 to 1934.
swap.clue: He ruled from 1918 to 1922 as the head of the military and seized power again in 1926, operating through such proxies as Jozef Beck and trying to appease Hitler until his 1935 death.

question.text: Mieszko conquered this former capital city that contained the Royal Wawel ("VAH-vel") Castle. Supposedly, a creature from this city named Smok Wawelski ("vah-VEL-ski") was tricked to eat sulfur-stuffed cow skins.
question.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

swap.text: Augustus William of Prussia allegedly died after a broken heart, but really died of a brain tumor, after a crushing defeat in this region. Prussia invaded this region of modern-day Poland to set off the war of Austrian succession.
swap.clue: Frederick the Great's 1740 occupation of this region triggered the War of the Austrian Succession.

question.leadin: This house lost power after the death of Casimir III the Great, the son of Wladyslaw the Elbow-High.
question.text: Name this dynasty founded by Mieszko I that ruled an oft-partitioned country in eastern Europe.

swap.leadin: Gallus Anonymus wrote a history of this dynasty, whose mythical founder was a wheelwright who succeeded the evil King Popiel after he was eaten alive by mice.
swap.text: Mieszko I ("m'YESH-ko the first") was the first historical ruler of what Polish dynasty?
swap.clue: Earlier, when this dynasty's ruler Henry II the Pious was killed at the Battle of Legnica, its Silesian branch was left exposed.

question.text: The Swedish monarchy was much more powerful a century earlier when it controlled Poland from 1655 to 1660 in a period known by this name
question.clue: Key precipitating factors of this period include the increased power of the nobility due to Sarmatism and Golden Liberty system, and it saw secondary conflicts like the Second Northern War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about medieval Lithuania.
swap.text: Vytautus had much better luck at this 1410 battle, where he ended the influence of the Teutonic Knights after attacking their fortress at Marienburg, leading to the Peace of Thorn.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of <u>Grunwald</u> [or First Battle of <u>Tannenberg</u>; or Battle of <u>Zalgiris</u>]
swap.clue: The Peace of Thorn showed the failure of the winning side to capitalize on this victory.

question.leadin: Name the following about leaders of Lithuania.
question.text: This Lithuanian prince became King of Poland under the Union of Krewo [krevo] and founded a namesake dynasty that variously ruled Lithuania, Poland, Hungary, and Bohemia.
question.clue: This man concluded the Peace of Thorn after defeating Grandmaster Ulrich von Jungingen (OOL-rick von YOUNG-ing-in) of the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Grunwald.

swap.leadin: This man argued that it is "better to have a friend than a slave" in his seminal Essay on Diplomacy, which he wrote under the pseudonym "Philhellene" ("feel-eh-LEN").
swap.text: Name this man who founded the Historical and Literary Society in Paris. This man bought the Hotel Lambert, which lends its name to a faction of people led by this man that participated in the Great Emigration.
